title: Selvage Session Protocol — every event of `selvage/1`
description: The twelve events a server sends, with the params of each. Valid against PROTOCOL.md §6. Event `params` are flat objects; an event name a receiver does not know is ignored, like an unknown member.

peerList.description: The peers already in the room, excluding `self`. No order is promised, so a receiver must not depend on one.

anyEventName.description: An event name. The twelve below are defined by `selvage/1`; any other, including every `x.`-prefixed name, is ignored rather than refused (contrast `unknown_method`).

roomCreated.description: `room.created`: the reply to a `session.hello` that minted a room. The minting connection is the host and is told the invite token here and nowhere else.

token.description: Present only here: the token is echoed exactly once, to the connection that minted the room, and a host that may reclaim must keep it (§9.1).

roomJoined.description: `room.joined`: the reply to a `session.hello` that joined an existing room. It never carries `token` — not even to a host reclaiming its own room.

peerJoined.title: peer.joined
peerJoined.description: To the peers already present when a connection is seated. A guest joining produces this; a host reclaiming its room produces `host.attached` instead.

peerLeft.title: peer.left
peerLeft.description: To the remaining peers when a connection ends, including the host's: a host disconnect sends `peer.left` first and `host.detached` after it.

peerRenamed.title: peer.renamed
peerRenamed.description: To every peer, the one that renamed included, when a peer changes its own display name. It carries no `awareness_client_id`: the rename changes no awareness and the join is already known.

docOpened.title: doc.opened
docOpened.description: To every peer, the one that made the change included, when a peer opens a document. The response to the request carries the same `documents` list.

docClosed.title: doc.closed
docClosed.description: To every peer when a peer closes a document. `documents` is the room's set after the change, which is unchanged when another peer still holds the path open. A disconnect releases holds silently and announces nothing.

docGranted.title: doc.granted
docGranted.description: To every peer, the publishing host included, when the host publishes a grant; and to a joining connection immediately after its `room.joined` when the room's grant is non-empty (§6.3). It names no peer: the host is the only publisher. `paths` replaces the receiver's view of the room's grant — it is a snapshot, never a delta — and carries no content: a name in it is not a promise that a file exists, is readable, or is held by any peer.

hostDetached.title: host.detached
hostDetached.description: To the remaining peers when the host's connection ends. The room is fully usable during the grace period and dies when it expires.

grace_ms.description: The server's host-reconnect grace period, in milliseconds.

hostAttached.title: host.attached
hostAttached.description: To the remaining peers when a connection reclaims a room that is between hosts. It names whoever claimed the host role with the right token, which is not necessarily the host a peer remembers.

roomGone.title: room.gone
roomGone.description: To the peers left behind when a room is destroyed: its host stayed away for the whole grace period. The room is gone for good, and the connection is closed with 4003.

sessionError.title: session.error
sessionError.description: A fault that cannot be attached to a request id: a handshake refusal, an unreadable envelope, or a fatal error on a request, in which case a matching close code follows.
